XCOM 2 Gets Steam Controller Support, Bundle Offered at a Discount [game + controller, 40% off]
Well this might be the excuse I needed to buy a steam controller.
I actually did and I'm pretty impressed with it. The little touchpads are slick and I like the feedback they give.

Every game has Steam Controller support, this just looks like it would allow for in-game configuration instead of going through Steam to change your configuration. Neat, but not really a game changer in my opinion.

For the record, I have a Steam controller and love using it for games that I'd normally play with a keyboard & mouse.

I don't think the steam controller replaces a keyboard and mouse with the same level of precision, but it is a reasonable alternative in situations where a keyboard and mouse may not be ideal due to a need for surface space. It's definitely something that takes time and a bit of effort to get accustomed to.

In my experience, the worst part about it are the A,B,X,Y button positions which they inexplicably decided should be below and to the left of the touch pad instead of up and to the right like every other sane control layout.

"Those who would give up essential Liberty, to purchase a little temporary Safety, deserve neither Liberty nor Safety." -- Ben Franklin

Of course, he had no idea what was to become of our electronic networks. His view might have been different had he a glimpse into our present, but I doubt it. Anyway, I agree with that quote even though I currently have no practical need for privacy.

Privacy is one of the ultimate demonstrations of individual sovereignty. You probably would not be comfortable with me demanding knowledge of and logging your daily activities, why should it be any different with a government entity? Do we think politicians are above reproach or corrupt actions? When two individuals form a long term relationship (marriage, etc.) usually they try to live their lives together, they share, privacy is of no concern because there is trust. If such trust was possible with government then, sure, I would give up privacy in an attempt to work together towards the betterment of society, but when a wife/husband/etc betrays you, usually, you can walk away with a divorce...if the government betrays you...you're simply fucked. When you don't trust the government you only really have one shield of protection against potential corrupt action...and that's anonymity.
